1. Justin Jefferson gets an elite matchup this week against a 49ers defense that has played a ton of Cover 3/6 (59.5% rate) this season. Against Cover 3/6 this year, Jefferson is averaging 3.05 YPRR with a 0.33 TPRR. Additionally, since Week 6, the 49ers defense has struggled against the pass, ranking 25th in passing success rate allowed (47.5%) and 22nd in EPA/pass allowed (0.03). Given that the Niners defense is a passing funnel, I’m expecting a big game from Jefferson on primetime. It also helps that Kirk Cousins has emphasized he wants to get Jefferson the ball.

2. With Kenneth Walker out, Emmett Johnson is set up to have a monster day on the ground against a Cardinals defense that’s struggled to stop the run lately. Since Week 6, the Cardinals rush defense ranks 25th in rushing success rate allowed (44.5%), 22nd in EPA/rush allowed (−0.03), 27th in YBC/ATT allowed (1.67), and 25th in stuff rate (17.8%). Meanwhile, Emmett Johnson has been excellent in his limited role this season, averaging 3.02 YACO/ATT with an explosive run rate of 12.1%. As far as concepts go, 47.9% of Emmett Johnson’s rush attempts this season have come on man-gap concepts. The Cardinals defense is allowing a 55.5% success rate against man-gap this year. In a game where the Chiefs are favored by 16.5 points, Emmett Johnson should get plenty of opportunities to carry the ball. Additionally with Jaylon Moore and Trey Smith out, I’m predicting Eric Bieniemy will heavily lean on the ground game in this matchup.

3. Since Week 7, Tony Pollard is averaging 5.82 YPC on man-gap concepts. During that same time frame, the Cowboys rush defense has really struggled, allowing 6.17 YPC and owning a stuff rate of just 14.4%. Additionally, over the past month, the Titans offense has run 75 no-huddle plays, which should help Pollard’s production. I expect Tony Pollard to have a massive day on the ground in this matchup against his former team.

4. After missing the past five games with a thumb/turf toe injury, Kyle Monangai is set to return this week against the Saints. According to NFL insider Mike Garafolo, Kyle Monangai carried no injury designation on Friday’s injury report, meaning he should not be limited in any capacity this week. Now let’s dive into the matchup. Brandon Staley’s defense has really struggled to stop the run this season, ranking 28th in EPA/rush allowed (−0.01), 28th in rushing success rate allowed (43.9%), and 22nd in YPC allowed (4.34). Meanwhile, Kyle Monangai has been one of the more efficient running backs in the NFL this season, averaging a 14% explosive run rate and a success rate of 51.7%. As far as rush concepts go, 70% of Monangai’s rush attempts this season have come on zone concepts. The Saints defense is allowing 4.54 YPC with a 55.2% success rate allowed against zone concepts this year. With rain in the forecast and the Bears favored by double digits, Monangai should get a fair share of carries in this matchup. Additionally, as the season progresses, I see this Bears backfield split getting closer to 50/50 rather than Swift being the clear bell-cow back.

5. Jaylen Warren gets a sneaky matchup this week against an Eagles defense that’s struggled to stop the run this season. Since Week 6, the Eagles defense ranks 25th in EPA/rush allowed (−0.02), 19th in YPC allowed (4.26), and 18th in rushing success rate allowed (42.2%). Meanwhile, Jaylen Warren has been one of the more efficient running backs in the NFL this season, averaging a 54% success rate along with a ridiculous 0.25 MTF/ATT. As far as rush concepts go, 50% of Jaylen Warren’s rush attempts this season have come on man-gap. The Eagles defense has been mediocre at defending man/gap this year, allowing 4.11 YPC with a 53.1% success rate allowed. Additionally, the Eagles defense will be without Jordan Davis (traded away) and Zach Baun (back injury). In a likely favorable game script, Warren should thrive against a mediocre Eagles rush defense.

6. Cam Skattebo gets a brutal matchup this week against a Jaguars defense that’s been excellent against the run this season. Anthony Campanile’s defense ranks 1st in EPA/rush allowed (−0.14), 1st in rushing success rate allowed (36.5%), 8th in YPC allowed (3.88), and 4th in YACO/ATT allowed (2.47). Meanwhile, the Giants rushing offense since Week 4 has been mediocre, ranking 17th in rushing success rate (40.5%) and 23rd in YPC (3.92). As far as rush concepts go, 56% of Cam Skattebo’s rush attempts this season have come on man-gap concepts. Why is that significant in this matchup? The Jaguars defense has been elite at defending man-gap this year, allowing just 3.61 YPC with a 46.1% success rate allowed. Additionally, with the acquisition of Jordan Davis, I’m expecting the Jags run defense to get back to the level they were playing at with Davon Hamilton in the lineup. In a likely trailing game script, I’m expecting the Giants offense to rely more on McCarthy’s arm in this game.

7. Deebo Samuel gets a difficult matchup this week against a Vikings defense that’s been running a ton of two-high shells (68.2% rate) this season. Against Cover 2/4/6 this year, Samuel is averaging just 1.15 YPRR with a 0.13 TPRR. With the Vikings defense ranking 1st in EPA/DB (−0.14) and 1st in passing success rate allowed (37.7%), I’m not expecting Samuel to do much in this matchup. Also, the 49ers offense is set to get Mike Evans back this week, and with Keenan Allen likely running more routes, Deebo Samuel’s target share is likely to drop. You typically want to back Deebo against teams that run a ton of one-high, not when they run two-high. Additionally, Kyle Shanahan’s game plan in this matchup is going to heavily revolve around the run game, as he doesn’t want Brock Purdy in obvious passing downs against Brian Flores’ blitz looks. So I’m super low on Samuel’s production as a receiver in this game.

8. Jaylen Waddle gets a favorable matchup this week against a Raiders defense that has struggled in coverage this season. Rob Leonard’s coverage unit this season ranks 32nd in passing success rate allowed (52.2%) and 30th in EPA/pass allowed (0.17). Now let’s dive into the coverage matchup. From a coverage standpoint this season, the Raiders defense has primarily operated out of one-high on 48.9% of dropbacks. Against Cover 1/3 this year, Jaylen Waddle is averaging a 0.31 TPRR with a 29.1% first-read share. Coming out of the bye week, I’m pretty optimistic about Waddle’s production in the second half of the season.

9. It took Jim Harbaugh and Mike McDaniel 10 weeks to make Omarion Hampton the bell-cow back, but finally in Week 10, Hampton played 63% of the Chargers’ offensive snaps. Now heading into Week 11, Hampton is set up to have another good performance against a Jets defense that’s struggled to stop the run without T’Vondre Sweat. When Sweat has been off the field this year, the Jets defense is allowing 4.8 YPC with a 48.7% success rate allowed, compared to 3.54 YPC and a 37.4% success rate with him on the field. Additionally, the Jets defense ranks 28th in the NFL this season in YBC/ATT allowed (1.71). So I’m expecting Hampton to find a decent amount of success on the ground in this matchup.

10. Over the past three seasons, Josh Allen has averaged just 5.8 rush attempts and 26.8 rushing yards per game in regular-season games where the Bills were favored by more than 10 points. However, when the Bills were favored by fewer than 10 points, those averages rose to 7.0 rush attempts and 35.2 rushing yards per game. (The Bills are favored by 16.5 points this week.) Additionally, the Bills have a game on deck on Thanksgiving, so I’m not expecting Joe Brady to run Josh Allen much in this matchup. There’s also a chance Kyle Allen takes some knees at the end of this game.

11. The Bucs defense ranks 32nd in the NFL this season in pressure rate (33%). Meanwhile, the Lions offensive line this year ranks 4th in pass-block win rate (58%). So I’m expecting Jared Goff to operate in a clean pocket for the most part in this game, which sets up Jameson Williams to catch a deep ball. Against Cover 3 this year, Williams owns a 17.35 ADOT along with a 38.7% air-yard share. (The Bucs defense has run Cover 3 at the highest rate in the NFL this season at 51.8%.) In a game where the Lions run game will likely be neutralized, I’m expecting Jameson Williams to catch at least one deep ball.

NFL Week 11 Preview

49ers vs. Vikings (Sunday Night Football, Mexico City)
- Kyle Shanahan vs. Brian Flores is as good of a coaching matchup as there is.

- I watch a lot of isolated night games as if I’m the middle linebacker. One of the reasons I do this is to see how often play callers can fool me. Over the last five years Shanahan has called drives where he’s had me on ice skates, which is a combination of him not only making me take the wrong first step at an abnormal rate, but he keeps you off balance by making you worry about everything. Like a pitcher changing speeds. That specifically is why I’m looking forward to this matchup, to see his approach against Flores, who is one of the few defensive play callers that dictates games in today’s NFL.

- The way Flores pairs coverage with the amount of frequent pressure he brings is remarkable. Getting Deebo Samuel in space on quick hitters/ hot reads would make sense. If Mike Evans plays, giving him, a very reliable player, a 50/50 ball or two paired with some timing pattern outs could create a little margin, I’ve thought that a timing, out breaking comeback could work against Minnesota against a lot of their pressure packages this season, but you can’t mess with that kind of thing, in those stressful environments, unless you have someone as reliable as Evans. I’d also expect Shanahan to roll Brock Purdy out to his right on one of the first plays of the game. In fact, I could see Shanahan moving the pocket at an abnormal rate against Flores.

- I’ll be curious to see how George Kittle and Christian McCaffrey are used as blockers. The could see the two of them creating margin by blocking and then releasing.

- What makes this game especially interesting is Kirk Cousins could conceivably help Minnesota hang in a game that San Francisco scores 24 or more points, where the Vikings would have been dead in that environment with Carson Wentz.

- San Francisco’s pass rush could be a problem in this matchup, and I don’t really view this as a good matchup for Minnesota running backs.

- I could see Justin Jefferson having his best game of the year on Sunday night.

- Whatever happens here, I’m not going to overreact to the outcome, especially with this game being played on a neutral field in Mexico City.

Bears vs. Saints
- The Bears are coming off their bye, which followed a very rocky game against the Bucs, where Chicago now has an extremely clean injury report on offense. I would be surprised if Chicago doesn’t score at least 30 points, and it would not stun me in the slightest if they put up a preposterous number against the Saints given the clean injury report, coming off a bye, that came after a very uneven offensive performance against Tampa.

- The question here is what kind of game does Tyler Shough have?

- Bears nickel corner Kyler Gordon is out again, so I could see Jordan Tyson having a good game.

- I could also see Chris Olave winning on a deep route against either Jaylon Johnson or Tyrique Stevenson (especially Stevenson) if Kellen Moore catches Chicago in the right coverage. Stevenson in particular, who is a pretty good third corner, will sometimes get caught cheating on a slant, and letting someone get over the top of him when there isn’t safety help.

- Before Chicago acquired Jeffery Simmons, I could have seen the Saints having a good enough game on offense to keep this mildly interesting. But now, given the optionality Simmons affords Dennis Allen (who I don’t think will give Shough layups over the middle). I could see this being over early, where the Saints get some garbage time production.

- Speaking of Simmons, the Saints are without their center Erik McCoy. Also speaking of Simmons, the Olave over the top situations are less likely now, as Chicago does not need to manufacture pressure as they did earlier in the year.

Cowboys vs. Titans
- Cam Ward played his best game of the season two games ago against the Bengals, and last week off Tennessee’s bye he had a relatively solid performance against Jacksonville. Dallas is bad enough to lose this game if Ward plays well again.

- If Carnell Tate returns this is a very high upside matchup for him.

- One thing I’ll frame in a positive light about the Cowboys’ defense is their pass rush had a very good game against San Francisco last week. Mike Pettine will call the plays for the Cowboys’ defense on Sunday, and historically he is big on disguise and bringing pressure creatively.

- Tennessee’s defense is atrocious now, where I could see Dallas smashing them in both phases. In particular, this looks like a plus game for Cowboys running back Javonte Williams. I’m not crazy about him as a player, but the Cowboys’ offensive line should have a good game against the Titans.

Giants vs. Jaguars
- Weather could be a factor in this contest, but right now wind looks like it will be reasonable.

- I could see the Jaguars front four being impactful in this contest, with the Giants generally struggling on offense.

- I will be curious to see how quickly safety Jessie Bates assimilates into a new defense mid-season. Bates has been one of my favorite players in the league for years, but incorporating a back-end player midseason is not as easy as having a front player, like Jordan Davis, join a new unit.

- The Giants best shot to generate offense is to move Malik Nabers around, manufacture a few touches for him, try to get him in some good matchups by lining him up everywhere, while keeping most things simple for J.J. McCarthy, given the impact Jacksonville’s front will likely have. But do I have faith in Matt Nagy doing what I think he should? Not so much.

- Arvell Reese and Abdul Carter are young, high-end defensive players. But the idea that Kayvon Thibodeaux is “doing the dirty work” super important player is hilarious to me. Every NFL player plays assignment football. Former No. 5 overall picks are taken to be impact players, he isn’t one. New York has two young stars on its front, but Thibodeaux isn’t one of them and they’ve been a disappointing pass rush as a group this season.

- New York’s secondary, in particular safety Jevon Holland and corners Deonte Banks and Greg Newsome II, have been an improvement this year. They could reasonably matchup with Jacksonville’s similarly tiered pass catchers, with the caveat that Trevor Lawrence is a top 10 quarterback and how well he plays in this game, will determine the game script in East Rutherford.

Bills vs. Dolphins
- Buffalo has a trench advantage in both phases, where their pass rush in particular should make descent rookie quarterback Kyle McCord speed up his internal clock (which is a negative).

- Once again, this would be a nice matchup to see some ceiling from Josh Allen’s passing attack.

- To Miami’s credit, they have been scrappy and have definitely gotten better since opening day, but this is a game Josh Allen’s crew should win comfortably, though comfortably doesn’t necessarily mean by three scores.

Chiefs vs. Cardinals
- It looks like Josh Johnson will start at quarterback for Arizona, where he’ll be supported by Trey McBride, a bad offensive line, and an atrocious wide receiver group with Michael Wilson out.

- Patrick Mahomes had a monster game against Atlanta last week, and he’s in a position to have another one of those against Arizona.

- Emmet Johnson will start in place of injured Kenneth Walker.

Broncos vs. Raiders
- I liked what I saw out of Fernando Mendoza in the first half of his debut last week, against a high-end defense in Seattle. My concern there is the same in this matchup, I think Mendoza is a player, but he’s dealing with a major roster disparity against Denver.

- It would make sense if this passing attack went through Brock Bowers (who is on the injury report) and Ashton Jeanty, as Denver has a trench advantage and their secondary is back against the Raiders well below average wide receiver room.

- Denver is a contender if they can get their offense right, so with them coming off their bye I’d expect some purposeful usage from Jaylen Waddle, because he’s the guy that can elevate them from who they were last year.

- This is a good matchup for Jonah Coleman.

Lions vs. Buccaneers
- I’d put this game largely on Detroit’s coaching staff.

- If Tampa can get to Jared Goff early, his internal clock will speed up and he becomes a very different player in those situations. If he’s kept relatively clean, Detroit is a lot to handle for any defense.

- I’ve been impressed by Tampa’s perimeter corners against bigger receivers, so I’m very curious to see how they fair against Amon-Ra St. Brown (route running) and Jameson Williams (speed), paired with Jahmyr Gibbs checkdowns in space.

- Jalon Daniels isn’t a very good quarterback, but he’s mobile and he can make plays against bad defenses. Detroit is down their two best defensive players in Aidan Hutchinson and Jack Campbell.

Eagles vs. Steelers
- Saquon Barkley, DeVonta Smith and the Eagles strong left side of their offensive line are off the injury report.

- A good game plan with Joe Milton could reduce Pittsburgh’s ability to create havoc up front, where the Eagles could keep this close behind a traditional muddy game plan given their injury report.

- Jordan Davis is in Jacksonville and Zack Baun is out, making this an interesting matchup for Steelers’ running backs.

- It would be nice if DK Metcalf landed a big play or two, that’s very overdue.

Panthers vs. Ravens
- If you were to ask me which ugly game has the most shootout potential, it’s this one. Quarterbacks that have 300 yard passing potential, neither team has a plus pass rush, and both teams secondaries are missing starters (some due to injuries, in one case, due to stupidity).

- Backup quarterbacks tend to hyper target top options, so I could see Zay Flowers having a nice game, with Carolina’s corners still sidelined.

- Derrick Henry saw 5 targets in Jacoby Brissett’s Ravens debut last week, so that should continue, and the offense should certainly run through The Big Dog and Flowers.

- After a good first month, Bryce Young has been largely mediocre since. That said, he has some interesting upside in this matchup, as does Tetairoa McMillan and Jalen Coker.

- As I pointed out before the season, the continuous, multi-year hype on Coker is absolutely ridiculous, but he is a solid role player that could do well here, assuming Baltimore gives McMillan the star treatment he often gets.

Chargers vs. Jets
- Geno Smith is off the injury report, so the Jets are very live to win this game as Smith is a very pressure sensitive quarterback, and the Chargers do not excel at generating pressure.

- New York has a better roster than the Chargers outside of quarterback and safety.

Commanders vs. Bengals (Monday Night Football)
- Joe Burrow and company should continue their hot streak of lighting up NFL defenses through the air, as their offensive line can mitigate Washington’s below average pass rush and Cincinnati’s dynamic wide receiver duo is a group the Commanders are not equipped to handle.

- Cincinnati’s front four has a trench advantage in this contest.

- Washington has a few things that I like. The first is I’d take Dan Quinn over Zac Taylor. The second is the Commanders are still alive in the NFC East. The third is Washington is coming off a long week.

- The final, and most important, is Jayden Daniels is capable of carrying a game, and he showed in his rookie year that he can win a primetime shootout against the Bengals.

I have watched every NFL game for roughly a decade. I have done this for the purpose of sports speculation.

I run a reality-based program here.

Engagement is how I reach new users. So as long as engagement remains strong (comments/ shares) I’ll continue pumping this and similarly detailed insights out every week.

The $ANT IPO was solid.

1) For the company, the IPO was great. They raised more money than they original thought with the both the amount of shares offered and IPO price increased.

2) The stock closed up 17% which is above the 10-15% threshold to call an IPO of this size successful.

3) The not so great news is the stock opened at +34% peaked a few minutes thereafter at +39% and then closed at +17%. A successful IPO sees the stock close higher than the open. This shows that investors who did not get an allocation are more eager to buy than those looking to sell the initial IPO pop and in this case, now that they finally have liquidity.

4) This decline in Anthropic’s stock over the day is likely the cause of the S&P going from up 1.3% in the morning to flat at the 11:49AM open of the IPO to down 2.0% by the close.

5) The real test of whether this was a successful IPO will come over the next 30 days during the green shoe window. Does the stock stays above its $83 IPO price in a tough tape for AI related stocks? I am not so sure.

Longer-term positives for Anthropic:

1) The value of frontier models increased with the US mid-term election of more pro regulatory politicians.

2) The CEO of $NVDA was the biggest proponent of open-weight models. With him gone, the potential for regulatory capture by Anthropic and OpenAI increases.

3) Anthropic was focused on day one on enterprises who are willing to pay vs OpenAI that focused on consumers who are used to getting internet services for free like search.

4) There is scarcity value in Anthropic being the first pureplay LLM that investors have and it is likely to be fast tracked into the indices.

5) The total available market of knowledge work was estimated at $40 trillion in 2025.

Negatives:

1) Combined revenue growth for OpenAI and Anthropic are slowing from ~75% q/q in Q2 to ~50% in Q3

2) Price competition between OAI, Anthropic and open-weight seems to be increasing. OAI price cuts drove revenue growth from roughly 17% q/q in Q2 to 50% in Q3 but dropped Anthropic from 144% q/q to 47%. But both saw adjusted operating margins going lower as a result. Anthropic dropped from 19% in Q2 to 15% in Q3 while OAI losses increased from roughly $10.1B to $10.9B in Q3. Combined operating losses increased from roughly $7.9B in Q2 to $8.4B in Q3.

3) Open-weight models are good for 90%+ of tasks today and they are likely to only get better. Harnesses are increasingly being used. They pick the best model for the task which in most cases is open-weight. This is why cost per token has come down by over 60% since May though this has driven tokens up nearly 6x.

4) I believe that ultimately enterprises will gravitate towards the safety of the $MSFT ecosystem while consumers will access AI on their smartphones either through the iOS ($AAPL) or Android ($GOOGL) ecosystems. 

5) The end-users are likely to become indifferent to which model is picked to run their tasks which then would commoditize this LLM layer over time.

In summary: price competition is increasing, rev growth is slowing and operating margins are dropping for the two leading LLMs while capital commitments are massive. But the opportunity is massive as well and Agentic AI is in its nascency. If I had to pick one LLM that survives the commoditization of this layer, Anthropic would be it. But it is not a favorite of mine for AI overall in the near-term.

Rock formations that seem tailor-made for a fantasy film.

1 - Wheeler Park, Colorado.
2 - In the Mexican state of Oaxaca—formations that resemble waterfalls.
3 - "Goblins," Utah.
4 - Red Rock State Park, near Cantil, California.
5 - Hoodoos in Drumheller, Canada.

The conventional narrative states the following:
👇
These five images show striking geological rock formations created over millennia by erosion and mineral deposits. However, within the context of certain alternative historical theories—such as the "melted buildings" or "mudflood" hypotheses—these are often interpreted as the petrified or melted remains of ancient megastructures.

A detailed geological classification:
1. Wheeler Geologic Area (Colorado, USA): These towers and columns originated from volcanic tuff associated with the La Garita Caldera (formed approximately 25 million years ago). Layers of solidified volcanic ash, varying in hardness, were eroded unevenly by wind and water.

2. Hierve el Agua (Oaxaca, Mexico): These "petrified waterfalls" are not melted walls, but rather massive travertine deposits. Over millennia, spring water rich in calcium carbonate flowed down the cliffs, depositing white minerals—a process similar to the formation of stalactites and stalagmites in caves.

3. Goblin Valley State Park ("Three Sisters," Utah, USA): These "hoodoos" (earth pyramids) are composed of Entrada Sandstone. Because the upper rock layers are significantly harder and more resistant to erosion than the softer sandstone beneath them, these mushroom-like or figure-like "heads" remain standing. 

4. Red Rock Canyon State Park (Cantil, California, USA): Here, sedimentary rocks—consisting of sandstone and clay—meet darker layers of basalt and lava. Tectonic uplift, combined with strong desert winds and flash floods, has eroded the softer intermediate layers, causing harder rock blocks to slide downward.

5. Drumheller Hoodoos (Alberta, Canada): Located in the Red Deer River Valley, these sandstone pillars date back 70 to 75 million years (to the Cretaceous period). In this case, an exceptionally hard capstone made of ironstone protects the softer sandstone column beneath it from being washed away by rain and meltwater.
